theory.title: Modales de deducción y posibilidad en presente
theory.explanation: Usa must cuando estás casi seguro de que algo es cierto; can't cuando consideras que es casi imposible; y may, might o could cuando algo es posible pero incierto. Después de estos modales utiliza el verbo base o be + adjetivo/sustantivo.
theory.tip: Must = casi seguro; can't = casi imposible; may/might/could = posibilidad.

patterns.label: Modales de deducción y posibilidad en presente · 1
patterns.pattern: The presenter must be very experienced.
examples:
The presenter must be very experienced.
→ El presentador debe de tener mucha experiencia.

patterns.label: Modales de deducción y posibilidad en presente · 2
examples:
That story can't be true.
→ Esa historia no puede ser cierta.

patterns.label: Modales de deducción y posibilidad en presente · 3
patterns.pattern: The editor might know the source.
examples:
The editor might know the source.
→ Puede que el editor conozca la fuente.

patterns.label: Modales de deducción y posibilidad en presente · 4
patterns.pattern: The audience may be waiting outside.
examples:
The audience may be waiting outside.
→ Puede que el público esté esperando fuera.

patterns.label: Modales de deducción y posibilidad en presente · 5
patterns.pattern: This could be the final episode.
examples:
This could be the final episode.
→ Este podría ser el último episodio.

patterns.label: Modales de deducción y posibilidad en presente · 6
patterns.pattern: The journalist must have good contacts.

The journalist must have good contacts.
→ El periodista debe de tener buenos contactos.

patterns.label: Modales de deducción y posibilidad en presente · 7
patterns.pattern: The rumour can't come from a reliable source.
examples:
The rumour can't come from a reliable source.
→ El rumor no puede proceder de una fuente fiable.

patterns.label: Modales de deducción y posibilidad en presente · 8
patterns.pattern: The producer might be planning a new series.
examples:
The producer might be planning a new series.
→ Puede que el productor esté preparando una nueva serie.

patterns.label: Modales de deducción y posibilidad en presente · 9
examples:
The headline may be misleading.
→ El titular puede ser engañoso.

patterns.label: Modales de deducción y posibilidad en presente · 10
patterns.pattern: They could be discussing the results now.
examples:
They could be discussing the results now.
→ Podrían estar hablando de los resultados ahora.

content.passage: A rumour about a popular presenter appeared online yesterday. Some viewers believe it must be true because several accounts shared it. However, the original source can't be confirmed, and the headline may be misleading. The editor might know more, but the newspaper has not published an official statement. The producer could be preparing a response. Until there is reliable evidence, readers should treat the story as uncertain.

items.prompt: Talk about a rumour and explain why it may or may not be true.
items.modelAnswer: I enjoy different kinds of media because they help me learn about the world and relax. I usually choose programmes that are informative and well presented. I also like discussing films and documentaries with friends because we often have different opinions. Although some online stories are not reliable, I try to check the source before sharing them. In the future, I think media will become more personalised, but good journalism will remain important.
